title: Object replication for block blobs
learningObjective: Configure object replication between storage accounts, meet its prerequisites, and explain how it differs from geo-redundant storage.
foundation: Object replication automatically copies block blobs from a container in one storage account to a container in another account, which can be in any region.
You choose the containers (and optionally a name prefix filter), unlike geo-redundant storage, which copies the whole account to a fixed paired region.
Copies happen in the background, a little after the original is written.
engineer: Prerequisites: blob versioning on both source and destination accounts, and change feed on the source. Hierarchical namespace accounts are not supported. Only block blobs are replicated; blobs in the Archive tier are not.

A replication policy (created on the destination first, then the source when done through the API/CLI) contains rules: source container → destination container, optional prefix filters, and whether to copy existing blobs or only new ones (a minimum creation time).
Replication is asynchronous, with no SLA on time. Replication status is shown per blob on the source (Complete/Failed).
While a policy is in place, replicated blobs in the destination container are read-only; writes fail.
Cross-tenant replication is disallowed by default on new accounts (AllowCrossTenantReplication = false).

Use cases: reduce read latency for users in another region, process data in a different region (compute near data), distribute data to several accounts, and optimise cost by replicating to an account with a different tier.

animation.caption: Open Object replication: satisfy the prerequisites, create the policy, and test what replicates.

example.title: Analytics in another region
body: Sales uploads data to stweu (West Europe). The analytics cluster runs in North Europe, so object replication copies the reports container to stneu, where the cluster reads it locally.
Only blobs with the prefix 'final/' are replicated, so work-in-progress files stay local.

permissions: Storage Account Contributor on both accounts (control plane)
limits: Destination blobs are read-only while the policy exists
portal: Source storage account > Data management > Object replication > Create replication rules.
Choose the destination subscription and account, then add container pairs and filters, and choose copy scope (only new objects, all, or since a date).
Verify per-blob replication status in the source container.
configuration.cli:
az storage account blob-service-properties update -g rg-data --account-name stweu --enable-versioning true --enable-change-feed true
az storage account blob-service-properties update -g rg-data --account-name stneu --enable-versioning true
az storage account or-policy create -g rg-data --account-name stneu --source-account stweu --destination-account stneu \
  --source-container reports --destination-container reports-copy --min-creation-time '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'
az storage account or-policy list -g rg-data --account-name stweu -o table
configuration.powershell:
Update-AzStorageBlobServiceProperty -ResourceGroupName rg-data -StorageAccountName stweu -IsVersioningEnabled $true -EnableChangeFeed $true
Update-AzStorageBlobServiceProperty -ResourceGroupName rg-data -StorageAccountName stneu -IsVersioningEnabled $true
$rule = New-AzStorageObjectReplicationPolicyRule -SourceContainer reports -DestinationContainer reports-copy -PrefixMatch 'final/'
$dest = Set-AzStorageObjectReplicationPolicy -ResourceGroupName rg-data -StorageAccountName stneu -PolicyId default -SourceAccount stweu -Rule $rule
Set-AzStorageObjectReplicationPolicy -ResourceGroupName rg-data -StorageAccountName stweu -InputObject $dest

lab.objective: Meet the prerequisites, create a policy and observe replication rules.
steps: Try to create the policy with nothing enabled and read the errors.
Enable versioning on both accounts and change feed on the source, then create it.
Upload Hot and Archive blobs, then try overwriting a replicated blob in the destination.
lab.cost: None in the simulation. Real replication incurs transaction and cross-region bandwidth charges and storage in both accounts.

troubleshooting.cause: Versioning or change feed is not enabled, or HNS is on.
troubleshooting.fix: Enable the prerequisites; use an account without hierarchical namespace.

troubleshooting.symptom: Some blobs show replication status Failed.
troubleshooting.cause: For example the blob is archived, or the destination container is missing or deleted.
troubleshooting.fix: Rehydrate or fix the destination; check status per blob.

troubleshooting.symptom: App writes to the destination container fail.
troubleshooting.fix: Write to the source, or remove the policy.

troubleshooting.symptom: Replication to a partner tenant fails.
troubleshooting.fix: Allow cross-tenant replication on both accounts if policy permits.

comparisons.difference: Whole account to the fixed paired region, secondary readable only with RA-; object replication is per container, to any account and region, and the destination is a normal readable account.
Very similar: requires versioning and replicates per bucket and prefix.
Manual or scheduled copies; object replication is continuous and service-managed.

misconceptions.myth: Object replication is a disaster-recovery failover feature like GRS.
misconceptions.reality: There is no account failover; it is asynchronous container replication.
Block blobs only, and not from the Archive tier.

architectureDecisions: Use object replication for data locality and distribution, and GRS/GZRS for account-level disaster recovery.
Filter by prefix to limit cost and replicate only finished data.

walkthrough.subtitle: Keep a copy of selected blob containers in another storage account, automatically.

steps.label: Copy needed
steps.title: Customers in another region read the same images
body: You want a copy of one container in another account, close to those customers, without writing a copy job.

steps.label: Replication
steps.title: Object replication copies block blobs for you
body: Object replication asynchronously copies block blobs from a source container to a destination container in another account, which can be in another region or subscription.

steps.label: Prereqs
steps.title: Turn on versioning and change feed
body: Blob versioning must be on in both accounts, and the change feed on the source account. The portal turns them on for you when you create the rules.

steps.label: Policy
steps.title: A policy holds the rules
body: A replication policy connects a source and a destination account. Each rule maps one source container to one destination container, optionally with a prefix filter and whether to copy existing blobs.
The destination container becomes read-only for writes while replication is set up.

callout.text: Object replication is not a backup. Deleting a blob in the source is replicated too (as a deletion of the current version).

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Object replication
body: Automatic, asynchronous copies of chosen containers.
recap: Needs versioning on both and change feed on the source

handsOn.title: Replicate a container to a second account
handsOn.cost: Cents. A few small files in a Standard LRS account cost almost nothing; delete the account at the end.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A storage account in rg-az104-lab: Standard performance, LRS redundancy, default settings. Name it st<yourinitials><number> (lowercase letters and numbers only, globally unique). This is the source.
A second storage account in the same group (the destination).

steps.do: In the source account create a container named images. In the destination account create a container named images-copy.
Open the source account > Data management > Object replication > Create replication rules.
steps.see: A form asking for the destination account and container pairs.

steps.do: Choose the destination account. Source container: images, destination container: images-copy. Copy over: everything. Create.
steps.see: A notice that versioning and change feed will be enabled. Accept it.

steps.do: Upload a small image or text file to images in the source account.
After 2–5 minutes open images-copy in the destination account.
steps.tip: Replication is asynchronous. If it is not there yet, wait a few more minutes.

steps.do: Try uploading a file directly into images-copy.
steps.see: The upload fails: the destination container is read-only while the policy exists.

check: A file uploaded to the source appeared in the destination.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
